notes: DECISIONS TAB WAS READING A FOURTH, UNCORRECTED CASH SERIES. REPORTED: with no scenarios enabled, a car decision showed liquidity of about Rs 11.42 L for April 2027 while the Projection and Net Worth pages showed about Rs 10.54 L for the same month. DIAGNOSED: _dcLiquidSeries built its liquidity from the engine's raw p.cashSeries, which carries none of the overlay corrections. On the reported data that raw series ran Rs 5,79,736 ABOVE the real chain. Two consequences followed. Decisions were judged against cash that is not there, so purchases looked more affordable than they are. And the figure reported WITH a car applied (Rs 11,42,925) exceeded the figure WITHOUT one (Rs 10,54,053) — buying a car appeared to leave more cash than not buying it. That impossibility is what identified the base series, rather than the purchase arithmetic, as the fault. FIXED: _dcLiquidSeries now reads projectSavingsChain, the same chain the Projection sheet, Dashboard and Net Worth use as of v2026.05.08.01, falling back to the raw series only if that call fails. Verified on a synthetic reproduction: with a car applied the decision sees Rs 6,36,051 against a no-car base of Rs 13,41,433, so cash falls when a car is bought, as it must. Performance unaffected — 11 ms per evaluation, 88 ms for a full earliest-feasible sweep. Regression confirms a zero gap between the Projection sheet and the Dashboard chain, and a zero gap between the Decisions liquidity series and that same chain. THIS IS THE FOURTH IMPLEMENTATION of the same quantity found in this codebase, after _eomSavingsChain (Projection), projectSavingsChain (Dashboard, Net Worth) and _liveLiquidCash (liquidity tiles). The first two were unified in v2026.05.08.01; Decisions was overlooked at the time and should have been included then. _liveLiquidCash stays separate by design, since it answers 'cash right now' rather than 'cash at month end'. There are now no known duplicate implementations of the month-end cash figure. EXPECT DECISION VERDICTS TO TIGHTEN, AND VERIFY THIS YOURSELF RATHER THAN TAKING THE NOTE ON FAITH: liquidity was previously tested against an inflated balance, so a decision that passed, or failed only narrowly, may now fail by considerably more and its earliest feasible month may move later. The size of that shift on real data has not been measured here. Engine, runProjection and the four decision tests themselves are untouched. No page errors.
